title: The Fallout of Using Array Indexes as Keys

blocks.content: Course: Build your First Web App with React
The Fallout of Using Array Indexes as Keys
So I tried deleting ItemA and modifying ItemB. To do that, I had to delete key 0 and then modify key 1. Here's what ended up happening:
As you can see, I wanted to modify ItemB but the code ended up modifying ItemC instead. All because the indexes shifted once ItemA got deleted.

blocks.alt: Don't Use Array Indexes as Keys

blocks.content: That's what happens when you set the index as your key. And this rookie mistake resulted in a frustrating debugging frenzy.
So heed my words and promise to yourself that you won't make this dumb mistake, ever! Trust me, it'll save you a lot of future sorrows.
And with that long story out of the way, let's get back to rendering our list 😎
